hypothesis: The frozen v51 entry gates are filtering after-cost noise rather than silently suppressing robust opportunities in the current live window.
correction: The prior continuous diagnostic ranked repeated route-level blocker rows. Exact portfolio episode-onset evidence is the independent unit. The corrected selector uses a unique episode attribution, refuses to pool long and short attributions, and no longer reports a robust HYPE missing-onset lead.
decision: Keep all v51 entry gates unchanged. Continue exact lifecycle and missed-opportunity measurement; do not reopen HYPE missing-onset or SOL hourly-cross relaxation from this evidence.
falsifier: Reopen a gate hypothesis only if a later predeclared compatible window has technically complete, side-separated independent episode onsets that remain positive after actual route costs and largest-winner removal, or if an eligible intent is suppressed outside the documented router contract.

SOL_missing_hourly_cross_60m.interpretation: The route-level row cannot pool independent long and short episode summaries into one promotion claim.

current_compatible_performance.interpretation: Descriptive current-run evidence only; four closes do not establish a repeatable portfolio edge.

recommendation.recommendation: Retain the exact v51 entry gates and continue forward measurement using episode-onset, side-separated opportunity units.
recommendation.why_now: The report-only monitor temporarily surfaced a HYPE research lead that disappeared when the independent sample definition was reconciled to the checkpoint's portfolio episode ledger.
evidence_reviewed: actual compatible lifecycle performance and costs
recommendation.observed_problem_or_opportunity: Persistent blocker rows were counted as route-level independent paths, overstating HYPE repeatability; SOL also has distinct long and short episode attributions that cannot be pooled.
recommendation.applicable_market_regime: Only the frozen v51 observation window and its observed regime mix; no claim is made for unobserved regimes.
alternatives_considered: pool long and short episode summaries
abort the entire digest on multiple side attributions
rank unique episode onsets and mark multi-side evidence as separation required
recommendation.expected_upside: Prevents false-positive research leads and avoids weakening live entry gates on concentrated evidence.
recommendation.main_risks_and_failure_modes: Episode samples remain sparse; counterfactual close marks are not executable fills; route costs may understate queue or impact; unique attribution depends on exact provider, symbol, blocker, side, and horizon identity.
recommendation.validation_completed: TDD covered unique episode ranking, ambiguous long/short attribution, legacy fallback, configured-route scope, and current live execution visibility; a real checkpoint one-shot produced zero robust leads.
recommendation.validation_still_required: Resolved live lifecycles on every route and side, actual fees/funding/slippage, non-adjacent regimes, and predeclared forward windows large enough to estimate repeatability.
recommendation.success_metrics: No repeated-row promotion; exact attribution count serialized; positive after-cost episode net and profit factor above one; positive after removing the largest winner; technical completeness; stable side-separated results.
recommendation.failure_or_rollback_triggers: Any diagnostic that promotes repeated blocker rows, pools ambiguous sides, or changes live authority is a defect; a later robust side-separated episode window updates the gate decision through a new reviewed revision.
recommendation.confidence_level: high for the diagnostic correction; medium for retaining gates in this window; low for long-run profitability

single_highest_value_next_investigation: Resolve the open exact-v51 SPCX short and reconcile its realized exit, MFE/MAE, profit-lock behavior, costs, and regime path.
limitations: The source checkpoint is rolling; the immutable digest freezes only the recorded prefix.
